intro: My research develops statistical tools for analysing time series whose behaviour changes over time. The applied questions are often in finance and in the sciences, where regime changes, shocks and non-stationarity are the central difficulty.

current.title: Spectral estimation for non-stationary time series
current.status: PhD research in progress, University of Bath, SAMBa Centre for Doctoral Training. Supervisor: [Matthew Nunes](https://mattnunes.github.io/).
current.summary: I am currently investigating estimates of spectral quantities for non-stationary time series, i.e. time series whose structure changes with time. I will also implement useful packages for calculating these in Python.

background.title: Near-critical percolation and branching processes
background.status: Earlier work, before I pivoted my focus to time series.
background.summary: Earlier work in probability theory on near-critical percolation and branching processes. Investigating critical behaviour on slabs with [Christoforos Panagiotis](https://sites.google.com/view/christoforos-panagiotis/). My Masters thesis on branching random walks with [Cécile Mailler](https://cecilemailler.github.io/). A summer project on the conformal invariance of the Abelian sandpile model with Antal Járai.
